history.summary: A genuine 1,421 sqft 4BR at Grandeur 8 — a large, liquid, well-located 579-unit AMK Central project with one of the better exit records in the OCR book (96.1% of 622 resales sold at a profit). The problem is the price, not the project: at $2.35M / $1,654 psf the ask tops every print this layout has ever made ($2.25M / $1,584 psf, Aug-25) and sits 6.8% above the freshest large-unit comp — a LARGER 1,453 sqft unit that sold for $2.35M-minus-$100k, i.e. $2.25M / $1,548 psf, on 27 Jul 2026, three weeks before this listing was cut. You would be paying a record price into a project with 37 units already competing for the same exit.
history.rating_rationale: The ask is above every comparable print, and the project's own recent history says so three separate ways. (1) LAYOUT RECORD: the exact 1,421 sqft 4BR has printed six times in the URA panel — $1,337, $1,358, $1,443, $1,478, $1,280 and $1,584 psf. The ask of $1,654 psf is +4.4% above its all-time high, and $2.35M tops even the $2.328M record for the whole 1,350-1,550 sqft band. (2) FRESHEST COMP: on 27 Jul 2026 a 1,453 sqft unit — 32 sqft LARGER — transacted at $2.25M / $1,548 psf. Same project, three weeks ago, $100k cheaper for more space. (3) SIZE-PSF INVERTED: among 15 live Grandeur 8 listings this is the 5th-largest unit but carries the 3rd-highest psf ask. The same $2.25M buys a 1,582 sqft 3BR/3-bath here; $2.49M buys 1,841 sqft. A large unit asking small-unit psf is backwards — PSF should fall with size, not rise. The 6.53% trailing CAGR that drives most of the algo's 624 is a size-mix artifact: segment the prints and the LARGE-unit tier is flat, not compounding. Same-size 1,453 sqft resale-to-resale runs Oct-23 $1,368 -> Oct-25 $1,525 -> Jul-26 $1,548 = 4.5%/yr and decelerating to ~2%/yr over the last nine months, while 2026's rising project median psf ($1,441 -> $1,498) is carried by the small 1,195-1,259 sqft stock (Mar-26 $1,557, Apr-26 $1,622, May-26 $1,564). Buying at $1,654 psf needs the large-unit tier to re-rate ~7% just to reach the ask. Note also that relative_value's -3.1% 'discount' to the age-adjusted D20 median is a sub-market artifact, not value: D20's $1,982 median psf is Bishan/Thomson on the TEL, and Ang Mo Kio Central's gap to it is a permanent location level that has never closed. MMR's own psf_value component (-4.9) already flags the ask as expensive; the 624 is carried by trailing appreciation (+7.6) that this repo's backtest values at ~zero forward power. The seller has already cut $2.43M -> $2.35M in 15 days and is still above every print — the direction is right and the level is not there yet. This flips to Neutral around $2.20-2.25M ($1,548-1,583 psf), i.e. a further $100-150k, and only then because the project itself is sound.

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Adequate but thin, and the weakest part of the case. URA gives $5,350/mo across 9 same-project 4BR contracts (confidence 0.90); realsmart's independent read is $3.64 psf avg rental and a 3.0% estimated yield, implying ~$5,170/mo — the two agree. On a $2.35M entry that is 2.73% gross and ~1.5% net, i.e. the hold is carried by the buyer, not the tenant. Grandeur 8's recent 12 rental contracts have a $4,550 median with a $3,850-$6,300 range, and the only 4BR contract visible in that window ($6,300) is on a 2,200-2,300 sqft unit, not this size. The 2-bathroom configuration is a real handicap in the 4BR rental market, where sharers and expat families price bathrooms directly. Demand itself is not the issue — AMK Central, two MRT lines by 2030 and two primary schools inside 1km keep the unit lettable — but at this price the yield does no work.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The headline 6.53%/yr (ura_5yr_cagr, 88 txns) does not survive size segmentation, which is the whole point. Grandeur 8 spans 1,109-2,314 sqft, and 2026's median-psf rise ($1,441 -> $1,498) is carried almost entirely by the small 1,195-1,259 sqft stock (Mar-26 $1,557, Apr-26 $1,622, May-26 $1,564). The large-unit tier this unit belongs to has gone sideways: the 1,453 sqft layout traced Oct-23 $1,368 -> Apr-25 $1,514 -> Oct-25 $1,525 -> Jul-26 $1,548, a clean same-size resale-to-resale series worth 4.5%/yr over 2.75 yrs and only ~2%/yr annualized over the last nine months. I have set the forward override to 4.5% on that segmented, same-size, resale-to-resale basis — and even that is measured entirely inside the 2021-26 bull regime, so treat it as a ceiling rather than a forecast. At $1,654 psf the buyer is roughly 7% ahead of the tier's own last print, which means the first two to three years of that 4.5% are spent recovering the entry premium before any real gain begins. The CRL interchange is genuine but arrives around 2030, at the far end of a 5-7yr hold, and the repo's panel finds no measurable forward power in future-infrastructure scores.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: No researched profile exists for Grandeur 8 (stack_profile: not_researched), and PropertyGuru serves no floor_level or facing for this listing — so the unit's floor is UNKNOWN, and that materially widens the range. It matters a lot here: the 1,421 sqft layout's own prints split hard by floor — $1,280 psf (Nov-24, floors 01-05) and $1,358 psf (Aug-23, 01-05) at the bottom against $1,478 psf (Sep-24, 16-20) and $1,584 psf (Aug-25, 11-15) at the top, a spread of roughly 24% on identical square footage. The ask of $1,654 psf is priced above the best floor band the layout has ever achieved, so it is only arguable at all on a high floor — and even a top-floor unit would be setting a project record. On a low or mid floor the ask is indefensible. The unit is in one of 20-storey blocks along Ang Mo Kio Central 3 (developer NTUC Choice Homes). Verify the floor and the outlook before any offer; if it is below the 11th storey, the gap to fair value is wider than the $100-150k quoted above. Running /research-development on Grandeur 8 would pay for itself given 15 live listings here.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: Size-segmented same-size resale-to-resale on the project's own large-unit tier (URA D20 prints + realsmart 27-Jul-2026 record): 1,453 sqft at $1,368 psf Oct-2023 -> $1,514 Apr-2025 -> $1,525 Oct-2025 -> $1,548 Jul-2026 = +13.2% over 2.75 yrs = 4.5%/yr. Replaces the pooled 6.53% ura_5yr_cagr, which is inflated by the small-unit (1,195-1,259 sqft) stock that drove 2026's median-psf rise. Bull-regime measurement — a ceiling, not a forecast.
